scope: esk-init skills mirror safety (ADR-0078, #130): re-mirror only changed/drifted skills; back up a diverged target before replacing (never silently delete); --check --skills fingerprints the target; the signature walk is split into signatureOf/skillSignature/targetSignature. No manifest-tracked file changed.

boundary.evidence: signatureOf is a correctly-factored shared walk; source-vs-target error policy (die vs null) sits at the right callers

ownership.evidence: marker is the single record; names:all fixes the orphan-on-remove bug; all source sigs stored as baseline, internally consistent

error-handling.evidence: THREE findings found and FIXED: (F1 HIGH) a pre-signature marker took no backup -> silent data loss on the first reconcile after upgrade; (F2 MED) --check reported a drift --yes could not clear; (F3 LOW) a present-but-unreadable target was replaced not stopped, contradicting the ADR. Fix: a baseline-agnostic classifyTarget drives backup (back up when sig != newSource && sig != recorded, so recorded=null still backs up), self-healing mirror (drifted targets re-mirrored so --yes clears --check), and die on unreadable. Proven by the reviewer's own repro scripts (SAFE / SELF-HEALED) + 3 new discrimination tests. 50/50 esk-init; full suite 732 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped.

notes: F1 (HIGH, data loss): the first reconcile after upgrading from a marker with skills.names but no skills.signatures had no recorded baseline, so the `recorded != null` backup guard was skipped and local content was deleted. FIXED: classifyTarget is baseline-agnostic - with no baseline it backs up any target that differs from the new source. New test starts from a signature-stripped marker and asserts the local file is preserved.

F2 (MEDIUM): --check --skills reported a source-unchanged-but-target-edited skill as drift, but it was never in the mirror set, so --yes printed 'nothing to change' and the gate stayed red. FIXED: drifted targets are included in the mirror set, so --yes re-mirrors them (backing up the edit) and the gate self-heals. New test: check(red) -> yes -> check(green).

F3 (LOW): a present-but-unreadable target fell through to replace, contradicting ADR-0078's 'the run stops'. FIXED: classify 'unreadable' -> die on the apply path. New capability-gated test (chmod 000; self-skips on Windows).

Honest limit recorded in the ADR: with no baseline (pre-signature marker) a stale-clean copy cannot be told from a local edit, so the first reconcile may back up a stale copy (conservative, one-time, never loses content); subsequent reconciles are precise. Original test 1 was re-purposed (its 'survives in place' premise is obsolete under self-healing - a diverged target is now backed up and re-mirrored); it now guards against spurious backups of clean skills.
